questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The revised guidelines / will be implemented / with immediate effect.
questions.x: The sentence is grammatically correct as written. The sentence is correct.

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech: 'I have told you a million times to save your files.'
questions.x: Correct answer: Hyperbole. Deliberate exaggeration.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The firm's precarious finances worried its lenders', the word 'precarious' means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Dangerously unstable. Precarious: not securely held, likely to fail.

questions.q: By the time the inspector arrived, the workers ____ the site.
questions.x: Correct answer: had already left. An earlier past action takes the past perfect.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The scenery of / the hill stations in the north / are breathtaking.
o: the hill stations in the north
questions.x: The error is in part (c): 'are breathtaking'. 'Scenery' is uncountable and singular: 'is breathtaking'.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The new manager told a story to break the ice at his first staff meeting', the idiom means:
o: To ease initial tension or awkwardness
To cool down an angry person
questions.x: Correct answer: To ease initial tension or awkwardness. Breaking the ice makes people more relaxed at the start.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The teacher said, "The Earth revolves around the Sun."
o: The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth was revolving around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth had revolved around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the Sun.
questions.x: Correct answer: The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun.. Universal truths keep the present tense.

questions.q:
Rearrange the following sentences (P, Q, R, S) to form a coherent paragraph:
P: Instead, it sets aside a portion of every salary.
Q: The scheme does not depend on the employer's goodwill.
R: This sum, along with interest, is returned at retirement.
S: The employer adds a matching contribution.
questions.x: 'Instead' must follow Q; S adds the employer's share; R explains the payout.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
Hardly (I had reached) the office when it started raining.
questions.x: Negative adverbs at the start take inversion: 'Hardly had I reached'.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
We look forward (to meet) you at the annual conference.
questions.x: Correct answer: to meeting. In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition and takes a gerund.

questions.q: What does the author consider more valuable than a document promising success?
questions.x: Answer: 'A drill that reveals weaknesses'. This is the final sentence. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Institutions are tested less in calm times than in crises. A disaster reveals whether information flows quickly from the field to decision-makers, whether agencies trust one another, and whether local officials are empowered to act without waiting for approval. Plans written in advance matter, but only if they have been practised. A drill that exposes failure is far more valuable than a document that promises success.

questions.q: According to the passage, a crisis reveals all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Whether citizens pay their taxes on time
Whether local officials can act independently
questions.x: Answer: 'Whether citizens pay their taxes on time'. Tax payment is not mentioned. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Institutions are tested less in calm times than in crises. A disaster reveals whether information flows quickly from the field to decision-makers, whether agencies trust one another, and whether local officials are empowered to act without waiting for approval. Plans written in advance matter, but only if they have been practised. A drill that exposes failure is far more valuable than a document that promises success.

questions.q: The passage suggests that written disaster plans:
o: Are useful only when they have been rehearsed
questions.x: Answer: 'Are useful only when they have been rehearsed'. 'Plans … matter, but only if they have been practised.' The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Institutions are tested less in calm times than in crises. A disaster reveals whether information flows quickly from the field to decision-makers, whether agencies trust one another, and whether local officials are empowered to act without waiting for approval. Plans written in advance matter, but only if they have been practised. A drill that exposes failure is far more valuable than a document that promises success.

questions.q: What is the author's view on administrative discretion?
o: It is necessary but should be exercised transparently
It is always abused by officers
It works best when decisions are kept confidential
It should be abolished in favour of strict rules
questions.x: Answer: 'It is necessary but should be exercised transparently'. The author says the answer is 'not to abolish discretion but to make it visible'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Rules exist because discretion can be abused, but no rulebook can foresee every case. An officer who follows the letter of a regulation while ignoring its purpose may be technically correct and practically unjust. The answer is not to abolish discretion but to make it visible: to require reasons in writing, to allow appeals, and to publish patterns of decisions so that arbitrary choices stand out. Discretion exercised in the open tends to discipline itself; discretion exercised in the dark tends to drift.

questions.q: Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the author's argument?
o: Departments that publish reasoned decisions see fewer successful appeals against arbitrariness
Officers who follow rules strictly are always promoted faster
Most citizens never read published decisions
Rulebooks have become longer every year
questions.x: Answer: 'Departments that publish reasoned decisions see fewer successful appeals against arbitrariness'. Evidence that transparency reduces arbitrariness supports the claim. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Rules exist because discretion can be abused, but no rulebook can foresee every case. An officer who follows the letter of a regulation while ignoring its purpose may be technically correct and practically unjust. The answer is not to abolish discretion but to make it visible: to require reasons in writing, to allow appeals, and to publish patterns of decisions so that arbitrary choices stand out. Discretion exercised in the open tends to discipline itself; discretion exercised in the dark tends to drift.

questions.q: The phrase 'discretion exercised in the dark tends to drift' means that hidden discretion:
o: Is replaced by written rules over time
Gradually moves away from fair and consistent standards
questions.x: Answer: 'Gradually moves away from fair and consistent standards'. 'Drift' suggests a slow move away from proper standards. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Rules exist because discretion can be abused, but no rulebook can foresee every case. An officer who follows the letter of a regulation while ignoring its purpose may be technically correct and practically unjust. The answer is not to abolish discretion but to make it visible: to require reasons in writing, to allow appeals, and to publish patterns of decisions so that arbitrary choices stand out. Discretion exercised in the open tends to discipline itself; discretion exercised in the dark tends to drift.

questions.q: Which of the following princely states posed special problems at the time of integration and required action beyond the Instrument of Accession process?
questions.x: Hyderabad (Operation Polo, 1948), Junagadh (plebiscite, 1948) and J&K (accession after invasion, 1947).

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wahabi movement — Sir Syed Ahmad Khan
questions.x: Faraizi — Haji Shariatullah; Wahabi — Syed Ahmad of Rae Bareli; Birsa — Munda Ulgulan.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the HSRA:
1. It was formed in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi.
2. Its members threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929 to protest against repressive bills.
3. It was founded by Rash Behari Bose in Tokyo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Rash Behari Bose was associated with the Indian Independence League in East Asia.

questions.q:
Match the woman freedom fighter with her association:
Person:
A. Aruna Asaf Ali
B. Captain Lakshmi Sahgal
C. Matangini Hazra
D. Usha Mehta
Association:
1. Hoisting the flag at Gowalia Tank, 1942
2. Tamluk, Quit India Movement
3. Congress Radio
4. Rani of Jhansi Regiment, INA
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Aruna Asaf Ali) → 1 (Hoisting the flag at Gowalia Tank, 1942); B (Captain Lakshmi Sahgal) → 4 (Rani of Jhansi Regiment, INA); C (Matangini Hazra) → 2 (Tamluk, Quit India Movement); D (Usha Mehta) → 3 (Congress Radio).
Women's roles in 1942 and the INA.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Shivaji's administration:
1. The Ashtapradhan was a council of eight ministers.
2. Chauth was a levy of one-fourth of the revenue of an area.
3. The Peshwa was the commander-in-chief of the army.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Peshwa was the chief minister; the Senapati commanded the army.

questions.q: Arrange the following dynasties in chronological order of their rise: 1. Mauryas 2. Guptas 3. Kushanas 4. Palas
questions.x: Mauryas (4th c. BCE), Kushanas (1st–3rd c. CE), Guptas (4th–6th c. CE), Palas (8th c. CE).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Montagu Declaration of 1917 marked a shift in British policy.
Reason (R): It announced the gradual development of self-governing institutions with a view to responsible government in India.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: Arrange the following reform organisations in order of founding: 1. Arya Samaj 2. Brahmo Samaj 3. Ramakrishna Mission 4. Prarthana Samaj
questions.x: Brahmo (1828), Prarthana (1867), Arya (1875), Ramakrishna Mission (1897).

questions.q:
Which of the following were part of the Non-Cooperation programme (1920)?
1. Surrender of titles and honours
2. Boycott of government schools and law courts
3. Boycott of elections to councils
4. Breaking the salt law
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Breaking the salt law was part of Civil Disobedience (1930).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Chola period:
1. The Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur was built by Rajaraja I.
2. Uttaramerur inscriptions describe village assemblies.
3. The Cholas are known for bronze sculpture such as Nataraja.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Delhi Sultanate:
1. Alauddin Khalji introduced market control measures.
2. Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced token currency.
3. Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka and copper jital.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Match the painting school with its feature:
School:
A. Mughal (Jahangir period)
B. Kangra
C. Kishangarh
D. Madhubani
Feature:
1. Naturalistic studies of birds and animals
2. Rajasthani paintings including 'Bani Thani'
3. Pahari paintings of Radha–Krishna in soft, lyrical lines
4. Folk paintings of the Mithila region
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Mughal (Jahangir period)) → 1 (Naturalistic studies of birds and animals); B (Kangra) → 3 (Pahari paintings of Radha–Krishna in soft, lyrical lines); C (Kishangarh) → 2 (Rajasthani paintings including 'Bani Thani'); D (Madhubani) → 4 (Folk paintings of the Mithila region).
Each school has a distinctive style and patronage.

questions.q:
Consider the following about financial regulators:
1. Sanjay Malhotra became Governor of the RBI in December 2024.
2. Tuhin Kanta Pandey became Chairman of SEBI in 2025.
3. Madhabi Puri Buch was given a second term as SEBI Chairperson.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Her term ended in February 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following maritime laws enacted in 2025:
1. The Bills of Lading Act, 2025
2. The Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 2025
3. The Merchant Shipping Act, 2025
Which of the above were enacted?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
They replaced colonial-era shipping laws.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): BRICS expanded its membership in 2024 and 2025.
Reason (R): Countries such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Indonesia joined as members.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies:
1. It entered into force in September 2025 after acceptance by two-thirds of members.
2. It prohibits subsidies for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
3. India accepted the agreement before it came into force.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India had not accepted it, seeking more policy space for its small fishers.

questions.q:
Consider the following about incentives under the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana:
1. First-time employees registered with EPFO can get one month's EPF wage, up to ₹15,000.
2. The employee incentive is paid in two instalments.
3. Employers get up to ₹3,000 per month for each additional employee, for employees earning up to ₹1 lakh a month.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
The second employee instalment is also linked to completing a financial-literacy programme.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): In 2025 the United States imposed additional tariffs on several Indian goods.
Reason (R): The US linked part of the additional duty to India's purchases of Russian oil.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. In August 2025 the US raised duties on many Indian goods to 50%, including a 25% penalty linked to Russian oil imports.

questions.q: India's first indigenously developed antibiotic for drug-resistant community-acquired pneumonia, launched in 2024-25, is:
questions.x: It was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC support; bedaquiline is an older anti-TB drug.

questions.q:
Match the 2025 Nobel Prize with its laureate(s):
Prize:
A. Peace
B. Literature
C. Chemistry
D. Economic Sciences
Laureate:
1. Kitagawa, Robson and Yaghi (metal–organic frameworks)
2. Mokyr, Aghion and Howitt (innovation-driven growth)
3. László Krasznahorkai
4. María Corina Machado
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Peace) → 4 (María Corina Machado); B (Literature) → 3 (László Krasznahorkai); C (Chemistry) → 1 (Kitagawa, Robson and Yaghi (metal–organic frameworks)); D (Economic Sciences) → 2 (Mokyr, Aghion and Howitt (innovation-driven growth)).
2025 Nobel laureates.

questions.q:
Consider the following anniversaries marked in 2025:
1. 150 years of 'Vande Mataram', written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
2. The 150th birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
3. The 150th birth anniversary of Birsa Munda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three were commemorated in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): India won the men's cricket Asia Cup in 2025.
Reason (R): The 2025 Asia Cup was played in the T20 format in the UAE.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; R gives the format and venue, not why India won.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Shubhanshu Shukla's spaceflight in 2025:
1. It was part of the Axiom-4 commercial mission.
2. The crew travelled on a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft.
3. He became the first Indian to go to space.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Rakesh Sharma flew in 1984; Shukla was the first Indian on the ISS.

questions.q:
Consider the following about international bodies:
1. The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted by the World Health Assembly in 2025.
2. The United States announced its withdrawal from the WHO in 2025.
3. India withdrew from the WHO in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India remains a member.

questions.q: In 2025 a Presidential Reference under Article 143 was made after a Supreme Court ruling on timelines for:
o: Governors and the President acting on Bills passed by State legislatures
questions.x: The reference followed State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu (April 2025).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Uniform Civil Code is a Directive Principle rather than an enforceable right.
Reason (R): Article 37 makes Directive Principles non-justiciable.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Article 44 is in Part IV; Article 37 explains why it is not enforceable.

questions.q:
Which of the following are features of the Indian parliamentary system?
1. Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers
2. A nominal head of State
3. Fixed tenure of the executive independent of the legislature
4. Membership of ministers in the legislature
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
A fixed executive tenure is a presidential feature.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Finance Commission:
1. It is constituted every five years or earlier.
2. It recommends distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States.
3. Its recommendations are binding on the Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Recommendations are advisory, though generally accepted.

questions.q: A litigant wants to appeal against a High Court judgment in a civil matter that raises a substantial question of law of general importance. The appropriate route is:
o: Appeal to the Supreme Court on a certificate under Article 133 or by special leave under Article 136
Reference to the President under Article 143
questions.x: Correct answer: Appeal to the Supreme Court on a certificate under Article 133 or by special leave under Article 136. Articles 132–136 govern appeals.

questions.q:
Consider the following safeguards for the independence of the judiciary:
1. Salaries of Supreme Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. Their conduct cannot be discussed in Parliament except on a motion for removal.
3. Retired Supreme Court judges cannot plead before any court in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Articles 112(3), 121 and 124(7).

questions.q:
Consider the following about borrowing by States:
1. A State may borrow within India on the security of its Consolidated Fund.
2. A State indebted to the Centre needs the Centre's consent to borrow.
3. States can borrow directly from abroad without any restriction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Article 293; States cannot borrow abroad directly.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Preamble:
1. The 42nd Amendment added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity'.
2. In Kesavananda Bharati the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution.
3. The Preamble can be enforced in a court like a Fundamental Right.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Preamble is a key to interpretation but is not enforceable on its own.

questions.q:
Match the subject with the List in the Seventh Schedule:
Subject:
A. Banking
B. Police
C. Forests
D. Public health and sanitation
List:
1. State List
2. State List
3. Concurrent List
4. Union List
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Banking) → 4 (Union List); B (Police) → 2 (State List); C (Forests) → 3 (Concurrent List); D (Public health and sanitation) → 1 (State List).
Forests moved from the State to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment.

questions.q:
Consider the following about national emergency under Article 352:
1. It can be proclaimed on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
2. The proclamation must be approved by both Houses by a special majority within one month.
3. During its operation, Article 19 is automatically suspended for all grounds of emergency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Article 19 is suspended automatically only when the emergency is on grounds of war or external aggression.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the removal of the Vice-President:
1. A resolution is passed by the Rajya Sabha by a majority of all its then members and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
2. At least fourteen days' notice of the intention to move the resolution is required.
3. The grounds for removal are specified in the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Constitution prescribes no grounds for removal of the Vice-President.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Delimitation Commission:
1. Its orders have the force of law and cannot be called in question in any court.
2. Lok Sabha seat allocation among States is frozen on the basis of the 1971 census until the first census after 2026.
3. It is a permanent constitutional body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Delimitation Commissions are set up under Acts of Parliament as needed.

questions.q:
With reference to the Rajya Sabha, consider the following:
1. It is not subject to dissolution.
2. The Deputy Chairman is elected from among its members.
3. The Vice-President votes in the Rajya Sabha on all questions as its Chairman.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Chairman has only a casting vote in case of a tie.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Article 15(3) allows special provisions for women and children.
Reason (R): Equality under Article 14 permits reasonable classification on an intelligible differentia with a rational nexus to the object.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true. R explains the general doctrine of classification under Article 14, but A rests on the specific enabling clause in Article 15(3).

questions.q: Budget data (₹ crore): Revenue receipts 43,000; Non-debt capital receipts 5,000; Revenue expenditure 55,000 (of which interest payments 14,000); Capital expenditure 9,000. The revenue deficit is:
questions.x:
Total expenditure = 55,000 + 9,000 = 64,000.
Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts) = 64,000 − 48,000 = 16,000.
Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest = 2,000.
Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts = 12,000.
Answer (revenue): ₹12,000 crore.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A depreciating rupee can widen India's merchandise trade deficit in the short run.
Reason (R): India's imports, such as crude oil, are relatively price-inelastic, so their rupee cost rises immediately.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. This is the J-curve effect.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes:
1. Incentives are linked to incremental sales of goods manufactured in India.
2. They cover sectors such as electronics, pharmaceuticals and automobiles.
3. They provide a one-time subsidy on land purchase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
PLI is output-linked, not a land subsidy.

questions.q:
Consider the following about NITI Aayog:
1. It replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
2. It is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
3. It brings out the SDG India Index ranking States and UTs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
It was set up by a Cabinet resolution; it is neither constitutional nor statutory.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the accrual concept:
1. Outstanding expenses must be recognised in the year to which they relate.
2. Income received in advance is shown as income of the year of receipt.
3. Prepaid expenses are shown as assets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
Income received in advance is a liability, not income of the year of receipt.

questions.q: After the year-end but before approval of accounts, a major debtor is declared insolvent; the debt existed at the year-end. Under the standard on events after the reporting period, this is:
o: A non-adjusting event to be disclosed only
An extraordinary item of the next year
An adjusting event — the provision for bad debts should be updated
questions.x: Correct answer: An adjusting event — the provision for bad debts should be updated. It provides evidence of a condition existing at the reporting date.

questions.q: A ship is damaged by sea water entering through a hole made by rats. The insurer pays because the 'proximate cause' is:
questions.x: The dominant effective cause of the loss is the sea water, a peril insured against (classic marine illustration).

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 200 units @ ₹10; 10th — 100 units @ ₹12; 20th — 250 units @ ₹16. 500 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 50 units left come from the latest purchases: 50 × ₹16 = ₹800.

questions.q:
Consider the following about depreciation methods:
1. SLM charges an equal amount every year.
2. WDV charges a higher amount in earlier years.
3. WDV can reduce the book value to zero after the useful life.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
A fixed rate on a reducing balance never reaches zero.

questions.q: If the auditor concludes that misstatements are material and pervasive (not merely a scope limitation), the opinion is:
o: Unmodified opinion with emphasis of matter
questions.x: Correct answer: Adverse opinion. Adverse: the statements do not give a true and fair view.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹60,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹1,500; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹5,000; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹350. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹60,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 1,500
− Cheques deposited not credited 5,000
− Bank charges 350
Pass book balance = ₹56,150.

questions.q: A, B and C share profits 2:2:1. C retires and his share is taken by A and B in the ratio 3:2. The gaining ratio and new ratio of A and B are:
P and Q share profits in the ratio 5 : 1. They admit R for a 1/4 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:

Which of the following errors will NOT affect the agreement of the trial balance?
1. Omitting a credit sale entirely from the books
2. Posting the same amount to the wrong account on the correct side
3. Recording repair expenses in the Machinery account
4. Undercasting the sales book
How many of the above will NOT affect the agreement?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Undercasting the sales book affects only the Sales account side, so the trial balance disagrees; the first three are complete omission, error of commission and error of principle.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹4,500 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 12% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 4,500 = ₹54,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 54,000 × 12% × 6/12 = ₹3,240.

questions.q: Which of the following situations involves an 'unfair labour practice' by the employer under the IR Code?
o: Refusing to recognise a union that has only 8% membership as the negotiating union
Declaring a lawful lock-out after giving notice
Dismissing a worker after a properly conducted domestic inquiry into theft
Transferring a union office-bearer to a distant place mala fide to weaken the union
questions.x: Mala fide transfer of a union office-bearer is an employer unfair labour practice listed in the Second Schedule; the others are lawful.

questions.q: Which of the following establishments is covered by the OSH Code regardless of the number of workers employed?
questions.x: Correct answer: A dock. Mines and docks are covered irrespective of employment size.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the four Labour Codes:
1. The Code on Wages received assent in 2019 and the other three Codes in 2020.
2. All four Codes came into effect on 21 November 2025.
3. Together they consolidate 44 central labour laws.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
They consolidate 29 central laws; some State laws and the Child Labour Act remain separate.

questions.q: Union X has 42% and Union Y has 23% membership in an establishment; Union Z has 19%. A dispute over the recognition result goes to:
o: The Industrial Tribunal, which adjudicates disputes between trade unions
questions.x: The IR Code gives Tribunals jurisdiction over inter-union disputes; here the council would comprise X and Y.

questions.q:
Consider the following under the Code on Wages, 2019:
1. The Central Government fixes a floor wage which States cannot undercut.
2. Minimum wages are to be reviewed or revised ordinarily within five years.
3. Overtime is payable at not less than twice the normal rate.
4. Minimum wages may differ for men and women doing the same work.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Statements 1–3 are correct. Gender-based differences for the same or similar work are prohibited.

questions.q:
Consider the following Articles and their content:
1. Article 23 prohibits begar and other similar forms of forced labour.
2. Article 24 prohibits employment of children below fourteen in factories, mines or hazardous employment.
3. Article 39(d) directs equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
4. Article 43B relates to participation of workers in management.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct; Statement 4 is incorrect.
Article 43B concerns promotion of co-operative societies; participation of workers is Article 43A.

questions.q: Workers serve a strike notice on 1 August. Conciliation begins on 5 August and fails on 20 August. Under the IR Code, the earliest date on which a lawful strike may begin is:
questions.x: Both conditions apply: not within 14 days of notice (i.e., after 15 August) and not during conciliation or within 7 days of its conclusion (20 August + 7 days). The later date governs — 28 August, still within 60 days of notice.

questions.q: A union negotiator first consults members to reconcile conflicting demands of senior and junior workers before meeting management. In Walton and McKersie's framework this is:
questions.x: Intra-organisational bargaining reconciles differences within one party.

questions.q: Which of the following best states the 'dominant nature test' applied in Bangalore Water Supply?
o: Where an organisation has both sovereign/non-industrial and industrial activities, the predominant nature of the activity decides whether it is an industry
questions.x: The Court looked at the predominant activity where activities are severable or mixed.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Asiad Workers' case (1982):
1. It was a public interest litigation.
2. It held that labour provided for less than the minimum wage due to economic compulsion is forced labour under Article 23.
3. It held that Article 24 applies to construction work, which is a hazardous employment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
The Court held construction work hazardous for the purposes of Article 24.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'protected' feature of an office-bearer of a registered trade union recognised as a protected worker during pendency of proceedings?
o: The employer cannot alter service conditions or dismiss the worker in connection with the dispute without permission
The worker is entitled to double wages
The worker cannot be transferred for any reason
questions.x: Protected workers are shielded from victimisation during pendency of proceedings.

questions.q: Which of the following situations does NOT entitle a woman to maternity benefit of 26 weeks under the Maternity Benefit Act, as amended?
o: She has two surviving children and expects a third
She expects her first child after working 85 days in the preceding year
She expects her second child and worked 90 days in the preceding year
She expects her first child and worked 120 days in the preceding year
questions.x: With two or more surviving children the entitlement is 12 weeks; the 80-day eligibility is met in the other cases.

questions.q: Arrange the following labour laws in chronological order of enactment: 1. Payment of Gratuity Act 2. Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act 3. Payment of Bonus Act 4. Equal Remuneration Act
questions.x: Payment of Bonus (1965), Contract Labour (1970), Payment of Gratuity (1972), Equal Remuneration (1976).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the National Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board under the OSH Code:
1. It is tripartite.
2. It replaces several advisory boards that existed under separate Acts.
3. It is chaired by the Chief Justice of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is constituted by the Central Government and chaired by the Secretary/Minister as notified — not the CJI.

questions.q:
With reference to the Code on Wages, 2019, consider the following statements:
1. The provisions on timely payment and authorised deductions apply to every employee, without any wage ceiling.
2. An employer may fix a wage period longer than one month if the employees agree in writing.
3. Where an employee resigns, the wages due must be paid within two working days of the resignation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
Wage periods may be daily, weekly, fortnightly or monthly — never longer than a month. The other two statements reflect Sections 16–17 of the Code.

questions.q:
Which of the following laws were subsumed in the Code on Social Security?
1. Employment Exchanges (Compulsory Notification of Vacancies) Act, 1959
2. Cine-Workers Welfare Fund Act, 1981
3. Payment of Bonus Act, 1965
4. Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
The Payment of Bonus Act went into the Code on Wages.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 26 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹330. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 26-week period including Sundays: 26 × 7 = 182 days.
Amount = ₹330 × 182 = ₹60,060. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹51,480.)

questions.q: An EPF member in continuous service dies. Average monthly wages over the last 12 months were ₹13,500 and the average balance in the member's PF account over that period was ₹2,50,000. The assurance benefit under the EDLI Scheme is:
questions.x:
EDLI = 35 × average monthly wages (ceiling ₹15,000) + 50% of the average PF balance (bonus capped at ₹1,75,000), subject to a minimum of ₹2.5 lakh and a maximum of ₹7 lakh.
35 × 13,500 = ₹4,72,500; bonus = min(50% × 2,50,000, 1,75,000) = ₹1,25,000.
Total ₹5,97,500.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A pay-as-you-go pension system uses current contributions to pay current pensions.
2. A fully funded system is more exposed to demographic ageing than a PAYG system.
3. A defined benefit scheme places investment risk on the sponsor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
PAYG systems are more exposed to ageing because fewer workers support more pensioners.

questions.q: An employee drawing monthly wages of ₹33,000 dies in an accident arising out of and in the course of employment. The relevant factor applicable to the deceased is 224. Taking the wage ceiling of ₹15,000 notified for computing compensation, the compensation payable is:
questions.x:
For death: 50% of monthly wages × relevant factor, subject to a minimum of ₹1,20,000.
Wages for computation = min(33,000, 15,000) = 15,000.
0.5 × 15,000 × 224 = ₹16,80,000 → payable ₹16,80,000.

questions.q: An establishment's EPF dues for March 2025 were deposited in late July 2025. Which combination of charges may EPFO levy?
o: Interest under Section 7Q and damages under Section 14B
Nothing, if the dues are paid before the financial year closes
questions.x: Both 12% simple interest (7Q) and damages (14B) on a graded scale apply to delayed remittance.

questions.q: A 38-year-old self-employed taxpayer wants a guaranteed government-backed monthly pension from 60. Which statement is correct?
o: She can join APY since the entry age limit is 50
She can join PM-SYM since there is no income limit
She cannot join APY because income-tax payers are ineligible; she may consider NPS
questions.x: APY bars taxpayers (since 2022); PM-SYM is for unorganised workers with income up to ₹15,000 aged 18–40; NPS is open to all.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the ESI Scheme:
1. Benefit periods follow contribution periods with a lag of three months.
2. Medical benefit is available to the insured person's family.
3. Employment injury benefits require a minimum of 78 days of contribution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Employment injury benefits are available from day one of insurable employment.

questions.q:
Consider the following about acid rain:
1. Rain with pH below about 5.6 is generally called acid rain.
2. It is caused mainly by oxides of sulphur and nitrogen.
3. Normal rain is perfectly neutral with pH 7.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Normal rain is slightly acidic (about 5.6) because dissolved CO₂ forms carbonic acid.

questions.q: Arrange the following in decreasing order of access speed: (1) CPU registers (2) Main memory (RAM) (3) Cache (4) Hard disk drive
questions.x: Correct answer: 1, 3, 2, 4. Registers are fastest, then cache, then RAM, then disk.

questions.q:
Consider the following about LIGO-India:
1. It is designed to detect gravitational waves.
2. It is being built in Hingoli district, Maharashtra.
3. It is an optical telescope for viewing distant galaxies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is a laser interferometer, not a telescope.

questions.q:
Consider the following about neem-coated urea:
1. Urea contains about 46% nitrogen.
2. Neem coating slows the release of nitrogen in the soil.
3. Neem coating makes it easier to divert urea for industrial use.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Neem coating discourages diversion to industry.

questions.q:
Match the disease with its vector:
Disease:
A. Malaria
B. Dengue
C. Kala-azar
D. Plague
Vector:
1. Female Anopheles mosquito
2. Sandfly
3. Rat flea
4. Aedes aegypti mosquito
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Malaria) → 1 (Female Anopheles mosquito); B (Dengue) → 4 (Aedes aegypti mosquito); C (Kala-azar) → 2 (Sandfly); D (Plague) → 3 (Rat flea).
Vector control is central to preventing these diseases.

questions.q:
Match the medical device or test with its principle:
Device:
A. MRI
B. CT scan
C. Ultrasonography
D. Pulse oximeter
Principle:
1. Echoes of high-frequency sound waves
2. Nuclear magnetic resonance of hydrogen nuclei
3. Absorption of red and infrared light by haemoglobin
4. Multiple X-ray images combined by computer
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (MRI) → 2 (Nuclear magnetic resonance of hydrogen nuclei); B (CT scan) → 4 (Multiple X-ray images combined by computer); C (Ultrasonography) → 1 (Echoes of high-frequency sound waves); D (Pulse oximeter) → 3 (Absorption of red and infrared light by haemoglobin).
Diagnostic tools based on physics.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Typing a website's name in a browser leads to the correct server.
Reason (R): The Domain Name System translates domain names into IP addresses.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. DNS is the 'phone book' of the internet.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the seasons on Earth:
1. They are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis.
2. The Earth is closest to the Sun in early January.
3. Summer in the Northern Hemisphere happens because the Earth is then nearest to the Sun.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Earth is nearest the Sun during the northern winter, showing that distance is not the cause.

questions.q:
Consider the following about a microwave oven:
1. It heats food mainly by making water molecules in it rotate rapidly.
2. Metal containers reflect microwaves and can cause sparking.
3. Microwaves make the food radioactive.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Microwaves are non-ionising radiation; they cannot make food radioactive.

questions.q:
Consider the following about permafrost:
1. It is ground that stays frozen for at least two consecutive years.
2. Its thaw can release carbon dioxide and methane stored in frozen organic matter.
3. Permafrost is found only in polar regions and not in high mountains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Mountain permafrost occurs in the Himalayas, Tibetan Plateau and Alps.

questions.q:
Consider the following about large language models (LLMs):
1. They are trained on large amounts of text to predict the next token in a sequence.
2. Most modern LLMs are based on the transformer architecture.
3. They always give factually correct answers because they look up a verified database.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
LLMs can produce confident but false statements ('hallucinations').

questions.q:
Consider the following about GM crops in India:
1. Bt cotton is the only GM crop approved for commercial cultivation.
2. GM mustard DMH-11 was approved for environmental release in 2022.
3. Bt brinjal is widely grown commercially in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Bt brinjal is under a moratorium in India since 2010 (it is grown in Bangladesh).

questions.q: In a certain code, 'A ÷ B' means A is the son of B; 'A @ B' means A is the father of B; 'A % B' means A is the brother of B. If 'K @ Q @ M' (read as K @ Q and Q @ M), how is K related to M?
questions.x:
K @ Q: K is the father of Q. Q @ M: Q is the father of M.
Combining the two (all persons taken to be of one family, as is conventional): K is the paternal grandfather of M.

questions.q: A bag has 8 white and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that at least one of them is white?
questions.x:
P(at least one white) = 1 − P(both black).
P(both black) = C(6,2)/C(14,2) = 15/91.
Required = 1 − 15/91 = 76/91.

questions.q: The mean of 7 observations is 70. If 6 of them are 87, 22, 42, 73, 40, 30, the remaining observation is:
questions.x:
Total = 7 × 70 = 490. Sum of known values = 294.
Missing = 490 − 294 = 196.

questions.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 382, 446, 1022 leaving the same remainder in each case.
questions.x:
If N leaves the same remainder, N divides the differences.
Differences: 446 − 382 = 64, 1022 − 446 = 576.
HCF(64, 576) = 64.

questions.q: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into cones of base radius 2 cm and height 6 cm. How many cones are obtained?
questions.x:
Number = volume of sphere / volume of one cone = (4/3)πR³ / ((1/3)πr²h)
= 4R³ / (r²h) = 4 × 6³ / (2² × 6) = 864 / 24 = 36.

questions.q: a clerk and an assistant together can digitise a set of records in 8 days. a clerk alone can do it in 12 days. How many days will an assistant alone take?
questions.x:
an assistant's one-day work = 1/8 − 1/12 = (12 − 8)/96 = 1/24.
So an assistant alone takes 24 days.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 8, 30, 17, 27, 26, 24, 35, ?
questions.x: Two interleaved series: odd positions 8, 17, 26, 35 (+9); even positions 30, 27, 24 (−3). The 8th term belongs to the even series: 24 − 3 = 21.

questions.q: The monthly incomes of P and Q are in the ratio 5 : 4 and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 3 : 1. If each of them saves ₹12,250 a month, P's monthly income is:
questions.x:
Let incomes = 5k, 4k and expenditures = 3m, 1m.
5k − 3m = 4k − 1m = 12,250 → 1k = 2m.
Solving gives k = 3,500, m = 1,750.
P's income = 5 × 3,500 = ₹17,500 (check: ₹17,500 − ₹5,250 = ₹12,250).

questions.q: A starts a business with ₹20,000. B joins after 7 months with ₹50,000, and C joins after 6 months with ₹25,000. Out of a year-end profit of ₹64,000, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 20,000×12, B: 50,000×5, C: 25,000×6 → 24 : 25 : 15.
B's share = 25/64 × 64,000 = ₹25,000.

questions.q: A cyclist rides from town P to town Q at 30 km/h and returns along the same road at 70 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.x:
For equal distances, average speed = 2uv/(u + v) (harmonic mean), not (u + v)/2.
= 2 × 30 × 70 / (30 + 70) = 4200/100 = 42 km/h.

questions.q: Given log₁₀ 2 = 0.301, how many digits are there in 2^27?
questions.x:
log₁₀(2^27) = 27 × log₁₀ 2 = 27 × 0.301 = 8.1270.
The characteristic is 8, so the number of digits = 8 + 1 = 9.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 4 : 9. After 5 years, the ratio will become 37 : 77. What is P's present age?

Production of a fertiliser unit (thousand tonnes) — 2017: 235  |  2018: 275  |  2019: 245  |  2020: 220  |  2021: 210.
What is the percentage change from 2017 to 2021?
questions.x:
Change = 210 − 235 = -25 on a base of 235 (earlier year).
% change = -25/235 × 100 = -10.64% → 10.64% decrease.

questions.q: Find the remainder when 5^115 is divided by 13.

Two inlet pipes can fill a storage tank in 10 hours and 40 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 12 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(10, 40, 12) = 120 units.
Rates: +12, +3, −10 units/hour → net 5 units/hour.
Time = 120 / 5 = 24 hours.

questions.q: The rent of a warehouse rises by 25%, then falls by 10%, and finally rises by 10%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 25/100) × (1 − 10/100) × (1 + 10/100) = 1.25 × 0.9 × 1.1 = 1.2375.
Overall change = (1.2375 − 1) × 100 = 23.75% → 23.75% increase.
Note: simply adding (25 − 10 + 10) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.
